The trans-Planckian, complex-structure/reheating, volume-dependence, convention-translation and large-extra-dimension/late-time questions have descriptions only in this case. The grouping therefore supports comparison without imposing a common dimension, vacuum sign or stabilization mechanism, inferring scientific identity from numerical membership, or establishing universal viability.

rows.originalText: The scope correctly separates vacuum existence, uplift, stability and scales. It accommodates the single-modulus limitations and purely perturbative alterna
rows.replacementText: The supplied passages support comparing vacuum existence, uplift, stability and particle scales as separate requirements. In the single-Kähler-modulus study, the complex-structure moduli are stabilized with the supersymmetry-breaking direction orthogonal to them, while the axio-dilaton may or may not participate in supersymmetry breaking. The source distinguishes this procedure from first integrating out presumed heavy dilaton and complex-structure fields. It reports supersymmetry-breaking minima with nearly zero cosmological constant, high gravitino and soft masses in the simplest cases, and a numerical example with a 10 TeV gravitino mass using several nonperturbative terms. For its stated h12 > h11 > 1 large-volume class, the 2005 source argues that (α′)^3 corrections and nonperturbative superpotential contributions produce nonsupersymmetric AdS minima with Kähler-sector supersymmetry breaking; its footnote allows some moduli to lie near the string scale despite the large total volume. The thesis summary reports volume-suppressed gravitino and soft scales and states a requirement for nonperturbative superpotential effects in Kähler stabilization. The supplied 2023 review separately reports a concrete orientifold lacking the divisor topologies needed for those effects, with entirely perturbative Kähler stabilization to AdS and D-term or T-brane uplift prescriptions. These different source statements do not establish a universal requirement for nonperturbative superpotentials. The bounded passages support the comparative question but do not certify full stability or controlled de Sitter vacua.

rows.replacementText: The supplied scope is supported as a comparison of local quivers embedded in compact IIB orientifolds with global brane consistency and moduli stabilization. The general fractional-D3 question in d2 remains description-only. The 2017 passages distinguish oriented quivers with exchanged singularities from orientifolded quivers and describe the roles of orientifold involutions, charge cancellation, gauge fluxes and stabilization ingredients. Their selected inflationary construction uses two geometric del Pezzo blow-up modes, one as the inflaton and the other to maintain volume stabilization. It focuses on transversally invariant divisors supporting O(1) instantons, leaving the exchanged-divisor U(1)-instanton option aside. The 2021 dP5 construction has its own requirements: a diagonal divisor that can shrink without forcing other divisors to shrink, and an involution under which it is transversely invariant and intersects the O7-plane. Its abstract reports a Higgsed and orientifolded local model embedded with tadpole and Freed-Witten anomaly cancellations, T-brane de Sitter stabilization and an MSSM low-energy spectrum. These reported constructions support the shared embedding question while retaining their distinct visible sectors, involutions, divisor conditions and cosmological targets. They neither identify every chiral quiver with a Standard Model construction nor establish inflation for every embedding; the supplied passages do not provide a complete consistency or control audit.

rows.originalText: EDE and late-time acceleration remain separate phases and questions. The specified EDE parameters are source targets, and the fourth challenge—explicit glob
rows.replacementText: The supplied scope appropriately keeps axion early dark energy and late-time acceleration as separate cosmological questions. The EDE source investigates C2 and C4 axion candidates in KKLT and LVS, targeting V = V0[1 − cos(ϕ/f)]³ with V0 approximately eV⁴ and f approximately 0.2 MP. Its requirements include controlled de Sitter stabilization, sufficiently heavy non-EDE modes, separation of the EDE scale from supersymmetry-breaking and gravitino scales, and natural microscopic parameters or enough freedom to implement any necessary tuning. The passages describe competing control requirements: large volume can help the expansions and EDE energy scale while lowering the decay constant and mass scales, whereas lowering nonperturbative prefactors at moderate volume introduces exponential tuning. The authors state that they address the first three challenges. The fourth requirement—an explicit globally consistent Calabi–Yau orientifold and brane setup permitting tadpole cancellation and all ingredients needed for stabilization and the EDE potential—is not established by the supplied passages. The source also leaves uncertain whether the D5 gaugino-condensation mechanism discussed for an earlier C2-axion proposal produces a nonzero superpotential contribution for cycles in the geometric regime. The separate one-or-two-large-extra-dimension question in d11 has description-only support and does not establish late-time acceleration or acceptable phenomenology.

The thesis summary reports a no-go theorem concerning QCD axions and supersymmetric moduli stabilization, and separately describes coexistence with nonsupersymmetric perturbative stabilization. Because the supplied summary gives neither the theorem's precise hypotheses nor its proof, it supports attribution of that reported result but not a universal exclusion or its application to an unspecified model. The 1206.0819v2 abstract dated 21 September 2012 reports, for natural background-flux values, an LVS axiverse containing a QCD axion and light ALPs with logarithmically hierarchical masses. It describes semi-realistic examples with stable moduli and an uneaten QCD-axion candidate, together with studies of masses, matter and gauge couplings, inflation-dependent cosmology and phenomenological constraints. The uneaten-candidate condition does not by itself establish that every strong-CP and phenomenological requirement is satisfied. The anomaly motivations and prospective searches remain source-dated statements; the supplied material establishes neither current observational status nor detailed quantitative viability.
